session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: To what extent do you support or oppose upzoning policies that allow for higher density housing in traditionally single-family neighborhoods? Please explain your reasoning.
column3: I am very opposed to upzoning policies for higher density housing in single family neighborhoods because I think it lowers the values of the homes. It ruins the aesthetic, it leads to overcrowding, and it adds a lot of stress on a system that isn't made for high density. For example, the neighborhood I live in is, you know, houses that are very spread out. We have nice wide streets, we have big lots. I don't want big buildings next to me. I pay a lot of money to live here and I don't especially want low-income housing in my high-income area.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: What do you think are the most significant impacts, positive or negative, of increasing housing density in residential neighborhoods?
column3: Biggest impact would be negative of overcrowding the schools, overcrowding the streets, leading to less parking, leading to higher crime and lowering the value of houses. The only positive is for people who can't afford to live here otherwise.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: How do you think upzoning policies might affect housing affordability in urban areas?
column3: Um, upzoning policies in an urban area is probably good. In urban areas they should be adding more housing because that's where a city is. It should not be in residential neighborhoods.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: What impact do you believe increased housing density might have on neighborhood character and quality of life?
column3: The character will go down, quality of life will go down, you will have non-families in family areas, you have crime, you're going to lose the ability to let your kids play outside because there's going to be an increase in crime.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: How do you think upzoning might affect transportation systems and traffic congestion in cities?
column3: I live in a smaller town. We don't even have public transportation. It would be a nightmare to add cars to the road. It would literally be awful for everyone.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: What role do you believe local government should play in regulating housing development and density?
column3: I think they should not be involved at all.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: How might environmental concerns factor into decisions about urban density and zoning?
column3: I think that the more you build, the worse it is for the environment. I say we keep our green areas and our trees and let our land have natural resources rather than just build, build, build.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: What economic effects, both positive and negative, might result from changing zoning laws to allow more multi-family housing?
column3: What ends up happening is the cost of living decreases where you are, so you're talking about people who have worked really hard their whole life to be able to afford a nice area, all of a sudden losing value in their homes and they'd probably leave and go somewhere where there wasn't upzoning.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: How do you think the interests of current residents versus future residents should be balanced when making zoning decisions?
column3: It should always be about current residents because they pay the taxes and they keep the city going. New residents should be moving to urban areas. If they can't afford a single-family home, then they need to not live in a residential suburban neighborhood.

session_1758603988672_fnjlos1: What role do you think social equity and access to opportunity play in discussions about zoning and housing policy?
column3: I don't believe in social equity and access to opportunity. I believe you work and you buy what you can afford and if you can't afford something you work harder.
